name: ET Fort Worth Basin Pipeline
researcher_notes: A natural gas trade news story from May 27, 2005 says Energy Transfer Partners put its 650 MMcf/d Fort Worth Basin Pipeline in service. It describes a 55-mile, 24-inch line from the Barnett Shale area that connects to the North Texas Pipeline in Johnson County, Texas. The EIA pipeline projects release for August 2026 (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 364, listed as 'ET Forth Worth Basin Pipeline') shows a completed new pipeline, in service June 2005, 54 miles, 24 inches, 650 MMcf/d, cost 53 million dollars, intrastate Texas. EIA is a separate publisher but not independent of the company announcement, so the tier is high from one validated source with a second that agrees. The length is staged as 55 miles from the news story; EIA says 54. The start point was not found in either source and is left blank. This is not an existing GEM row: the only nearby row is Hugh Brinson (P3885), which is a different, much longer line. An intrastate line, so no FERC filing is expected; the Texas Railroad Commission T-4 record was not checked. A 24-mile, 24-inch looping project (400 MMcf/d, in service May 2006, EIA Excel row 398, listed as 'ET Forth Worth Basin Looping') is about 38 km of new pipe, so it could be its own expansion row. It is not staged here because only EIA states it. The owner name follows the ownership team's style for an alias match (Energy Transfer LP). Route not researched: no official GIS found, so RouteType is left blank.
